title: I'll Buy or Sell SoFi After Earnings. Here's What Decides It
creator: Couch Investor
summary: Couch Investor previews SoFi's Q3 report, due Tuesday 27 October before the market opens, and sets out exactly what would make him buy more. The video opens with breaking news instead: Brazilian and South American names sold off pre-market — NU down 22.3%, MercadoLibre down 14.3% and dLocal down 9.7% (auto-captions garble MercadoLibre as 'Marcado Libra') — apparently after Lula won the presidency again; he says the political risk does not change his view, but advises letting the overreaction cool. He also dismisses Elon Musk's negative neocloud posts as talking SpaceX's book, calling Nebius world-class while saying CoreWeave just has to deliver. On SoFi itself, down about 50% in 12 months to under $15 with a $18.6 billion market cap, he predicts revenue of $1.28 billion against $1.25 billion consensus, adjusted EBITDA of $435 million, EPS of $0.17 and over a million new members. His DCF gives a bull case of $28, a base case of $22.80 and a bear case of $10 — about 51.3% upside. The call is conditional: he will buy more next week only if the report is extremely good and management assures investors it can still hit its targets; he is definitely not selling.

calls.stance_flip: Couch Investor was HOLD on SOFI (most recent tracked call, 9 Oct backfill entry), now CONDITIONAL_BUY — will buy more after earnings only if the report is strong and management gives assurance on its targets; explicitly not selling
calls.price_at_call: trading under $15 (stated); down ~50% over 12 months, ~55% drawdown from peak; market cap $18.6bn (stated); P/E 30x, forward 20x, PEG 0.5 (stated); his DCF bull $28 / base $22.80 / bear $10, ~51.3% upside on his assumptions
calls.thesis: CONDITIONAL_BUY — he will buy more SoFi shares next week if Q3 (Tue 27 Oct, pre-market) is an extremely good report and management assures shareholders it can still meet its own mid-term targets in a harsher rate environment; as of now he is waiting, and he is definitely not selling.
calls.base_case: His Q3 predictions: revenue $1.28bn (consensus ~$1.25bn), adjusted EBITDA $435m at a 34% margin (on track for the $1.6bn target), diluted EPS $0.17, over 1m new members at ~$322 acquisition cost; financial services ~$500m, lending ~$745m at a 56% contribution margin, Galileo ~$90m sequential growth; FY26 EPS guidance $0.60.
calls.bull_case: Bull DCF case $28/share (30% probability in his model): SoFi keeps beating consensus as it has in recent quarters (revenue beats of 7.1%, 3.6%, 3.1%; EPS beats of ~10%+) and management confirms the 30% growth compounding for the next ~2.5 years.
calls.bear_case: Bear DCF case $10/share (20% probability): management cannot deliver its targets, especially if the high-rate environment worsens into 2027; the stock was arguably too expensive near $30 at the start of the year, which he concedes may explain part of the 50% fall.
